body: Kula World is a PlayStation puzzle-platform game by Game Design Sweden AB, first released in Europe on 10 July 1998. The player guides a beach ball around suspended structures, collecting the keys needed to open an exit. Rolling across an edge changes the direction of gravity, turning another side of the same structure into the floor. A small collection of blocks can therefore contain several routes that are difficult to see at once. The game asks the player to understand an object by travelling around it rather than looking at it from one fixed side.

Coins and jewels reward exploration, while new obstacles make a direct route more complicated. Moving platforms, transporters and other devices change what can be reached from a particular position. The player has to connect these possibilities with the ball's changing orientation, remembering where an edge leads after the view has turned. A familiar surface may become useful only after approaching it from elsewhere. The challenge grows through combinations of these rules, so progress depends on building a reliable picture of the whole structure while controlling one small part of it.

Collecting fruit can unlock bonus stages, where every block must be activated by rolling across it. These levels give the same movement another objective and encourage a more complete exploration of their shapes. Twice a Man supplied the music, reinforcing the game's unusual atmosphere. North America received it as Roll Away, while the Japanese edition was called KulaQuest. It was Game Design Sweden AB's only video game. Its clear central idea remains distinctive: gravity changes at the edge, and the player's understanding has to turn with the ball.
